title: Optimization Solver — Overview and definition
description: Finds minima of linear, nonlinear, integer, and global optimization problems.
body: Signature edition. Signature-original methods and framings for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. Finds minima of linear, nonlinear, integer, and global optimization problems. An optimization solver minimizes objective functions subject to bounds and linear/nonlinear constraints, covering LP, QP, MILP, NLP, and derivative-free global search. Real implementations include HiGHS and CBC for linear/mixed-integer problems, IPOPT for nonlinear programming, and NLopt for global search. It reports optimality gaps, dual bounds, and certificates of infeasibility.
capabilities: Linear and mixed-integer programming with branch-and-bound
Nonlinear programming with interior-point and SQP methods
Global and derivative-free optimization (DIRECT, CMA-ES, Bayesian)
Multi-start strategies and automatic scaling of badly scaled models
Optimality certificates, gap reporting, and IIS infeasibility analysis

title: Optimization Solver — Actual implementation
description: Finds minima of linear, nonlinear, integer, and global optimization problems.
body: Signature edition. Signature-original methods and framings for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. How Optimization Solver is actually implemented. An optimization solver minimizes objective functions subject to bounds and linear/nonlinear constraints, covering LP, QP, MILP, NLP, and derivative-free global search. Real implementations combine Modeling APIs (PuLP, Pyomo, JuMP), solver C APIs, NL/ LP file readers, CLI with A simplex/interior-point core, presolve routines, BLAS/LAPACK. The implementation is verified by Verify on NETLIB LP and CUTEst NLP benchmarks: optimal values match reference optima within tolerance and infeasible models return certified IIS results

title: Optimization Solver — Teaching-ladder exercise
description: Finds minima of linear, nonlinear, integer, and global optimization problems.
body: Signature edition. Signature-original methods and framings for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. Teaching ladder for Optimization Solver, simple to complex. Rank 1: name the tool's single core action (Linear and mixed-integer programming with branch-and-bound). Rank 3: run it once on a tiny input and check the output. Rank 5: combine two capabilities: Linear and mixed-integer programming with branch-and-bound and Nonlinear programming with interior-point and SQP methods. Rank 7: chain its output into a neighboring tool (Numerical computation engine) with a verification checkpoint. Rank 9+: automate the full workflow and teach it to someone else.
